# Description
K-Nearest Neighbor classification of the feature vectors per character sequence (loaded from ~/results/features_combined.csv). The results are stored in ~/results/classifier/. KNN is strictly speaking not a machine "learning" algorithm. Given a data point in the test set, it simply takes the k-nearest neighbors (in the "training" set) of this data point, and assigns the majority label of these to it. See figure below. 

In the context of the current analyses, there are four relevant dimensions (instead of two as in the example below), namely, the TTR, unigram entropy, entropy rate, and repetition rate for the respective sequences. 

```{r foo, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Workings of the KNN algorithm, taken from https://ourcodingclub.github.io/tutorials/machine-learning/."}
knitr::include_graphics("~/Github/UpperPalCombinatorics/figures_external/knn.jpg")
```

# Load Data
Load data table with estimated feature values per sequence. 
```{r}
# load feature value estimations 
estimations.df <- read.csv("~/Github/UpperPalCombinatorics/results/features/features_combined.csv")
head(estimations.df)
```

Select subcorpora for binary classification.
```{r}
# choose subcorpora to compare: "Aurignacien", "TeDDi", "Cuneiform (Uruk V)",
# "Cuneiform (Uruk IV)", "Cuneiform (Uruk III)".
subcorpus1 <- "Aurignacien"
subcorpus2 <- "TeDDi"
selected <- c(subcorpus1, subcorpus2)
estimations.subset <- estimations.df[estimations.df$subcorpus %in% selected, ]
nrow(estimations.subset)

# downsample to have the same number of sequences across different combinations of corpora
# comment this out to use all the sequences (unbalanced across combinations of corpora)
estimations.subset <- sample_n(estimations.subset, 300)

# exclude sequences under a certain length
#estimations.subset <- estimations.subset[estimations.subset$num.tokens > 10, ]
```

Remove NAs (whole row)
```{r}
estimations.subset <- na.omit(estimations.subset)
```

# Normalization
Center and scale the data.
```{r}
# first four columns are meta information, the others are the feature values
# be aware that this needs to be changed in case of other table format
estimations.scaled <- cbind(estimations.subset[, c("subcorpus", "sequence", "num.tokens", "num.types")], 
                            scale(estimations.subset[, c("huni.chars", "hrate.chars", 
                                                         "ttr.chars", "rm.chars")]))
```

# Training and Test Sets
```{r}
# Generating seed
set.seed(09012020)
# Randomly generating our training and test samples with a respective ratio of 2/3 and 1/3
datasample <- sample(2, nrow(estimations.scaled), replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.67, 0.33))

# Generate training set (select rows randomly by using datasample vector)
train <- estimations.scaled[datasample == 1, 1:ncol(estimations.scaled)]
# Generate test set 
test <- estimations.scaled[datasample == 2, 1:ncol(estimations.scaled)]
# number of data points in test set
test.n <- nrow(test)
```

# Building KNN Classifier
Initialize data frame for storing results.
```{r}
knn.results <- data.frame(k = numeric(0), baseline = numeric(0), 
                          accuracy = numeric(0), accuracy.pvalue = numeric(0), 
                          precision = numeric(0), recall = numeric(0), 
                          f1 = numeric(0), test.n = numeric(0))
```

Run KNN classification.
```{r}
# choose maximum number of neighbors n
n = 10
# run a loop over different numbers of neighbors up to n
for (k in 1:n){
  # knn estimation of labels
  predictions.knn <- knn(train = train[, c("huni.chars", 
                                           "hrate.chars", 
                                            "ttr.chars", 
                                           "rm.chars")],
                         test = test[, c("huni.chars", 
                                           "hrate.chars", 
                                            "ttr.chars", 
                                           "rm.chars")], 
                         cl = train[, "subcorpus"], k = k) 
  
  # model evaluation
  # creating a dataframe from known (true) test labels
  test.labels <- test[, "subcorpus"]
  # combining predicted and known classes
  class.comparison <- data.frame(predictions.knn, test.labels)
  # giving appropriate column names
  names(class.comparison) <- c("predicted", "observed")
  # inspecting our results table
  head(class.comparison)
  # get confusion matrix
  cm <- confusionMatrix(data = class.comparison$predicted, 
                      reference = as.factor(class.comparison$observed))
  # print(cm)
  # get performance metrics from the output list of confusionMatrix()
  baseline <- cm$overall['AccuracyNull']
  accuracy <- cm$overall['Accuracy']
  accuracy.pvalue <- cm$overall['AccuracyPValue']
  f1 <- cm[["byClass"]]["F1"]
  recall <- cm[["byClass"]]["Recall"]
  precision <- cm[["byClass"]]["Precision"]
  
  # unname and round resulting values (except for p-values)
  baseline <- round(unname(baseline), 2)
  accuracy <- round(unname(accuracy), 2)
  f1 <- round(unname(f1), 2)
  recall <- round(unname(recall), 2)
  precision <- round(unname(precision), 2)
  
  # prepare data frame with results
  local.results <- data.frame(k, baseline, accuracy, accuracy.pvalue,
                              precision, recall, f1, test.n,
                              row.names = NULL)
  # print(local.results.rounded)
  knn.results <- rbind(knn.results, local.results)
  # give predictions alongside the other information in data frame
  knn.predictions.df <- cbind(test, predictions.knn)
  # write df with predictions for post-hoc analyses
  write.csv(knn.predictions.df, file =
              paste(c("~/Github/UpperPalCombinatorics/results/classifier/KNN/predictions/predictions_KNN_",
                                              subcorpus1, "_",
                                              subcorpus2, "_",
                                              paste("k", k, sep = ""),
                                              ".csv"), collapse = ""),
                                      row.names = F)
}
print(knn.results)
```

Write results to file. 
```{r}
# write results
write.csv(knn.results, file = paste(c("~/Github/UpperPalCombinatorics/results/classifier/KNN/performance/performance_KNN_",
                                              subcorpus1, "_",
                                              subcorpus2,
                                              ".csv"
                                              ), collapse = ""),
                                      row.names = F)
```
